description: Part single and part-two storey rear extension and rear dormer
decision_conditions: <p><span id="docs-internal-guid-5e26b9d6-7fff-36c5-136f-f47edada39c2"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;PT Sans&quot;, sans-serif; font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;">The proposed dormer, by reason of its bulk, size, scale and detailed design, would result in an obtrusive, unsympathetic, poorly designed and incompatible form of development. As such, the proposed development is considered contrary to paragraph 215 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policies D3 (Optimising Site Capacity Through the Design-Led Approach), D4 (Delivering Good Design) and HC1 (Heritage Conservation and Growth) of the London Plan (2021), Policies LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character) and LP3 (Designated Heritage Assets) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033, and Hackney's Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (2025). </span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-3ef8e88d-7fff-1cf6-92eb-44563465df69"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;">The proposed ground floor extension&nbsp;by reason of its scale, siting and proximity to the shared boundary, would result in significant adverse impacts on the residential amenity of the occupiers of No. 50 Durlston Road through an unacceptable loss of daylight, outlook, overbearing impact and an increased sense of enclosure. The proposal would therefore fail to provide an acceptable standard of amenity for neighbouring occupiers and is contrary to Policy LP2 (Development and Amenity) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 </span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-1355c4a0-7fff-b27f-2676-ca01773f9b60"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;">The proposed part single storey, part two storey rear extension, by reason of its excessive scale, bulk and siting, would comprise an unsympathetic and incongruous form of development that would fail to appear as a subordinate addition to the host dwelling, failing to preserve the significance of the Northwold and Cazenove conservation area. No public benefits have been identified that would outweigh the harm arising from the proposed development. The proposal is therefore contrary to </span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;PT Sans&quot;, sans-serif; font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;">paragraph 215 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024)</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;">, Policies&nbsp; D4 (Delivering good design) of the and HC1 (Heritage quality and standards) London Plan (2021), Policies LP1 (Design quality and local character) and LP3 (designed heritage assets)&nbsp; of the Hackney Local Plan 2033, and the guidance contained within Hackney's Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (2025).</span></span></p>
